# Palettes validated with the dataviz validator (scripts/validate_palette.js).
# Ordinal blue ramp, steps 250/350/450/550/650 — monotone L, all gaps >= 0.06.
PAL_STAGE <- c("#86b6ef", "#5598e7", "#2a78d6", "#1c5cab", "#104281")
# Categorical slots 1-3 — all-pairs CVD dE 9.2, normal-vision dE 24.0.

# ships direct value labels AND a table view (the relief rule).

INK_1 <- "#0b0b0b"; INK_2 <- "#52514e"; INK_3 <- "#8a8880"

theme_report <- function(base_size = 11) {
  theme_minimal(base_size = base_size) +
    theme(
      plot.title      = element_text(face = "bold", size = base_size + 1, colour = INK_1),
      plot.subtitle   = element_text(colour = INK_2, margin = margin(b = 10)),
      plot.caption    = element_text(colour = INK_3, hjust = 0, size = base_size - 2),
      axis.title      = element_text(colour = INK_2),
      axis.text       = element_text(colour = INK_2),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.major.x = element_line(colour = "#e8e7e3", linewidth = 0.3),
      legend.position = "top",
      legend.title    = element_text(colour = INK_2),
      legend.text     = element_text(colour = INK_2),
      strip.text      = element_text(face = "bold", colour = INK_1)
    )
}

```{r parsers}
#| include: false

# ---- one parser per upstream source; all return NA rather than guessing ----

parse_bowtie2 <- function(path) {
  out <- list(total = NA_real_, unaligned = NA_real_, uniq = NA_real_,
              multi = NA_real_, rate = NA_real_)
  if (!file.exists(path)) return(out)
  x <- readLines(path, warn = FALSE)
  g1 <- function(pat, s) {
    m <- regmatches(s, regexpr(pat, s, perl = TRUE))
    if (!length(m)) return(NA_real_)
    as.numeric(gsub("[^0-9.]", "", m))
  }
  ln_tot <- grep("reads; of these:", x, value = TRUE)
  ln_un  <- grep("aligned 0 times", x, value = TRUE)
  ln_u1  <- grep("aligned exactly 1 time", x, value = TRUE)
  ln_mu  <- grep("aligned >1 times", x, value = TRUE)
  ln_rt  <- grep("overall alignment rate", x, value = TRUE)
  if (length(ln_tot)) out$total     <- g1("^[0-9]+", trimws(ln_tot[1]))
  if (length(ln_un))  out$unaligned <- g1("^[0-9]+", trimws(ln_un[1]))
  if (length(ln_u1))  out$uniq      <- g1("^[0-9]+", trimws(ln_u1[1]))
  if (length(ln_mu))  out$multi     <- g1("^[0-9]+", trimws(ln_mu[1]))
  if (length(ln_rt))  out$rate      <- g1("^[0-9.]+", trimws(ln_rt[1]))
  out
}

parse_star <- function(path) {
  keys <- c(input = "Number of input reads",
            uniq_n = "Uniquely mapped reads number",
            uniq_p = "Uniquely mapped reads %",
            multi_p = "% of reads mapped to multiple loci",
            toomany_p = "% of reads mapped to too many loci",
            short_p = "% of reads unmapped: too short",
            other_p = "% of reads unmapped: other",
            mismatch = "Mismatch rate per base, %",
            maplen = "Average mapped length")
  out <- setNames(as.list(rep(NA_real_, length(keys))), names(keys))
  if (!file.exists(path)) return(out)
  x <- readLines(path, warn = FALSE)
  for (k in names(keys)) {
    ln <- x[grepl(keys[[k]], x, fixed = TRUE)]
    if (length(ln)) {
      v <- trimws(sub(".*\\|", "", ln[1]))
      out[[k]] <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(gsub("%", "", v)))
    }
  }
  out
}

parse_fastp <- function(path) {
  out <- list(in_reads = NA_real_, out_reads = NA_real_, too_short = NA_real_,
              lowq = NA_real_, manyN = NA_real_, dup_rate = NA_real_,
              q30_before = NA_real_, q30_after = NA_real_,
              len_before = NA_real_, len_after = NA_real_, version = NA_character_)
  if (!file.exists(path)) return(out)
  j <- jsonlite::fromJSON(path)
  out$in_reads   <- j$summary$before_filtering$total_reads
  out$out_reads  <- j$summary$after_filtering$total_reads
  out$q30_before <- j$summary$before_filtering$q30_rate
  out$q30_after  <- j$summary$after_filtering$q30_rate
  out$len_before <- j$summary$before_filtering$read1_mean_length
  out$len_after  <- j$summary$after_filtering$read1_mean_length
  out$too_short  <- j$filtering_result$too_short_reads
  out$lowq       <- j$filtering_result$low_quality_reads
  out$manyN      <- j$filtering_result$too_many_N_reads
  out$dup_rate   <- j$duplication$rate
  out$version    <- j$summary$fastp_version
  out
}

parse_dedup <- function(path) {
  out <- list(before = NA_real_, after = NA_real_)
  if (!file.exists(path)) return(out)
  d <- utils::read.csv(path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  gv <- function(k) {
    v <- d$count[d$metric == k]
    if (length(v)) as.numeric(v[1]) else NA_real_
  }
  out$before <- gv("before_dedup")
  out$after  <- gv("after_dedup")
  out
}
```

```{r collect}
#| include: false

samples <- read.delim("config/samples.tsv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
status  <- read.delim("logs/run_status.tsv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

geno_levels <- c("TUT4", "TUT7", "TUT4_TUT7", "DIS3L2", "MOV10", "WT")
geno_label <- c(TUT4 = "TUT4Δ", TUT7 = "TUT7Δ",
                TUT4_TUT7 = "TUT4/7Δ", DIS3L2 = "DIS3L2Δ",
                MOV10 = "MOV10Δ", WT = "WT control")

rows <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(samples)), function(i) {
  s  <- samples[i, ]
  pn <- s$pipeline_name
  bt <- parse_bowtie2(file.path("logs/align", paste0(pn, "_bowtie2_transcriptome.log")))
  bg <- parse_bowtie2(file.path("logs/align", paste0(pn, "_bowtie2_genome.log")))
  st <- parse_star(file.path("logs/align",  paste0(pn, "_Log.final.out")))
  fp <- parse_fastp(file.path("fastq_read2", paste0(pn, "_fp_report.json")))
  dd <- parse_dedup(file.path("R_output",   paste0(pn, "_deduplication.csv")))
  stt <- status[status$pipeline_name == pn, ]

  data.frame(
    pipeline_name = pn,
    planned_label = s$output_name,
    genotype      = s$genotype,
    replicate     = s$replicate,
    # --- wall time ---
    minutes = if (nrow(stt)) as.numeric(difftime(
      as.POSIXct(stt$finished[1], format = "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S"),
      as.POSIXct(stt$started[1],  format = "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S"),
      units = "mins")) else NA_real_,
    exit = if (nrow(stt)) stt$exit[1] else NA_integer_,
    # --- funnel ---
    r1_raw          = bt$total,
    r1_transcriptome = bt$total - bt$unaligned,
    umi_adapter     = fp$in_reads,
    fastp_pass      = fp$out_reads,
    dedup_after     = dd$after,
    dedup_before    = dd$before,
    # --- alignment ---
    bt2_tx_rate     = bt$rate,
    bt2_tx_uniq     = bt$uniq,
    bt2_tx_multi    = bt$multi,
    bt2_gn_rate     = bg$rate,
    bt2_gn_total    = bg$total,
    bt2_gn_uniq     = bg$uniq,
    bt2_gn_multi    = bg$multi,
    star_input      = st$input,
    star_uniq_p     = st$uniq_p,
    star_multi_p    = st$multi_p,
    star_toomany_p  = st$toomany_p,
    star_short_p    = st$short_p,
    star_other_p    = st$other_p,
    star_mismatch   = st$mismatch,
    star_maplen     = st$maplen,
    # --- QC ---
    fastp_dup       = fp$dup_rate,
    q30_before      = fp$q30_before,
    q30_after       = fp$q30_after,
    len_before      = fp$len_before,
    len_after       = fp$len_after,
    fastp_too_short = fp$too_short,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
})

m <- bind_rows(rows) %>%
  mutate(
    genotype  = factor(genotype, levels = geno_levels),
    geno_disp = geno_label[as.character(genotype)],
    dedup_rate = 1 - dedup_after / dedup_before,
    # retention at each funnel step, relative to the previous step
    ret_tx     = r1_transcriptome / r1_raw,
    ret_umi    = umi_adapter / r1_transcriptome,
    ret_fastp  = fastp_pass / umi_adapter,
    ret_dedup  = dedup_after / fastp_pass,
    ret_total  = dedup_after / r1_raw
  ) %>%
  arrange(genotype, replicate)

# stable sample ordering for every chart
m$pipeline_name <- factor(m$pipeline_name, levels = rev(m$pipeline_name))

fmt_n <- function(x) formatC(x, format = "d", big.mark = ",")
fmt_p <- function(x, d = 1) paste0(formatC(x * 100, format = "f", digits = d), "%")
```

## Outputs carry the original FASTQ stem

Every file this run produced — intermediates, logs and the three final outputs —
is named after the sequencing-facility FASTQ stem (`T7_14_S326`), not a friendly
label (`t7_2`). Renaming is a deliberately deferred step. The `planned_label`
column below records the intended label; **nothing has been renamed yet**.
:::

```{r overview-table}
#| echo: false

m %>%
  transmute(
    Sample = as.character(pipeline_name),
    `Planned label` = planned_label,
    Genotype = geno_disp,
    Rep = replicate,
    `Wall time (min)` = round(minutes, 1),
    Exit = exit,
    `Raw R1 reads` = fmt_n(r1_raw),
    `Final (deduplicated)` = fmt_n(dedup_after),
    `Overall retention` = fmt_p(ret_total)
  ) %>%
  arrange(match(Sample, rev(levels(m$pipeline_name)))) %>%
  kable(align = "llcrrrrrr")
```

# Read counts: in and out

The pipeline is **not a single funnel** — R1 and R2 take different routes — so
"reads in / reads out" needs stating precisely. The stages below follow the R1
read identity through the pipeline, since that is what determines which
fragments survive to the final table.

| # | Stage | Source | What it removes |
|---|-------|--------|-----------------|
| 1 | Raw R1 reads | bowtie2 transcriptome log | — (input) |
| 2 | R1 aligned to transcriptome | bowtie2 transcriptome log | reads not matching any transcript in the **full** transcriptome (all biotypes) |
| 3 | R2 mate carries UMI + adapter | fastp JSON, `before_filtering` | mates without the `[ATCGN]{15}GTCAG` motif |
| 4 | Passed fastp QC | fastp JSON, `after_filtering` | **length only** (`-l 80`). Quality filtering is off (`-Q`), so `low_quality_reads` is 0 in every sample |
| 5 | After deduplication | `*_deduplication.csv` | PCR duplicates, collapsed on the R1 transcript coordinate |

```{r funnel-chart}
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 9.5
#| fig-cap: "Reads surviving each stage, per sample. Bars within a sample are nested subsets, not additive parts."

stage_lv <- c("1. Raw R1", "2. R1 → transcriptome", "3. UMI + adapter",
              "4. Passed fastp", "5. After dedup")

fun_long <- m %>%
  select(pipeline_name, geno_disp,
         `1. Raw R1` = r1_raw,
         `2. R1 → transcriptome` = r1_transcriptome,
         `3. UMI + adapter` = umi_adapter,
         `4. Passed fastp` = fastp_pass,
         `5. After dedup` = dedup_after) %>%
  pivot_longer(-c(pipeline_name, geno_disp), names_to = "stage", values_to = "reads") %>%
  mutate(stage = factor(stage, levels = stage_lv))

ggplot(fun_long, aes(x = reads, y = pipeline_name, fill = stage)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.82), width = 0.76) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = PAL_STAGE, name = NULL) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = label_number(scale = 1e-6, suffix = "M"),
                     expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.04))) +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = 1, reverse = FALSE)) +
  labs(title = "Read counts through the pipeline",
       subtitle = "Millions of reads surviving at each stage",
       x = "Reads", y = NULL,
       caption = "Stages are nested subsets: every stage-5 read is also a stage-1 read.") +
  theme_report()
```

m %>%

    Sample = as.character(pipeline_name),

# Alignment statistics

Three independent alignments run per sample:

- **R1 → transcriptome** (bowtie2, **end-to-end**, `--no-unal`) against the **full**
  transcriptome, `fasta/index_bowtie_full_transcriptome/full_trans_` — 670,670
  sequences spanning every biotype, rRNA and lncRNA included, not the 112,218-sequence
  protein-coding index that also exists on disk. Assigns the fragment to a gene and
  supplies the deduplication coordinate.
- **R2 → AT-masked genome** (STAR, `--outFilterMultimapNmax 20`,
  `--outFilterScoreMinOverLread 0.50`). **The only source of a tail measurement** — the
  soft clip *is* the tail — and the source of the coordinates behind `loc_status`.
- **R2 → unmasked genome** (bowtie2, end-to-end) against GRCh38 primary. Contributes
  **no tail and no coordinate**. It is the templated-sequence flag: a read that aligns
  end-to-end over its full length has no non-templated segment, so an apparent tail on it
  is genomic. Feeds `al_ete_bt` and `bt_nm_over_tail` only.

> Because R1 is aligned against the **full** transcriptome, rRNA-derived fragments are
> assigned a gene on the R1 side. Their R2 mates then land in the rDNA repeat arrays,
> which is why multimapper handling on the R2 side matters so much — see
> `docs/TAIL_CATEGORIES.md`.

```{r align-chart}
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 9
#| fig-cap: "Alignment rates. Values are direct-labelled because one series colour sits below 3:1 contrast on a light surface."

aln_lv <- c("bowtie2 → transcriptome (R1)", "bowtie2 → genome (R2)", "STAR → masked genome (R2), unique")

aln_long <- m %>%
  select(pipeline_name,
         `bowtie2 → transcriptome (R1)` = bt2_tx_rate,
         `bowtie2 → genome (R2)` = bt2_gn_rate,
         `STAR → masked genome (R2), unique` = star_uniq_p) %>%
  pivot_longer(-pipeline_name, names_to = "metric", values_to = "pct") %>%
  mutate(metric = factor(metric, levels = aln_lv))

ggplot(aln_long, aes(x = pct, y = pipeline_name, fill = metric)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.82), width = 0.74) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.1f", pct)),
            position = position_dodge(width = 0.82),
            hjust = -0.18, size = 2.9, colour = INK_2) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = PAL_CAT, name = NULL) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = label_percent(scale = 1),
                     limits = c(0, 112), breaks = seq(0, 100, 25),
                     expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.01))) +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = 2)) +
  labs(title = "Alignment rates by sample",
       subtitle = "Percent of reads entering each aligner",
       x = "Alignment rate", y = NULL) +
  theme_report()
```

```{r align-table}

m %>%
  transmute(
    Sample = as.character(pipeline_name),
    Genotype = geno_disp,
    `R1 in` = fmt_n(r1_raw),
    `bt2 tx rate` = sprintf("%.2f%%", bt2_tx_rate),
    `bt2 tx uniq` = fmt_n(bt2_tx_uniq),
    `bt2 tx multi` = fmt_n(bt2_tx_multi),
    `R2 in` = fmt_n(bt2_gn_total),
    `bt2 genome rate` = sprintf("%.2f%%", bt2_gn_rate),
    `STAR in` = fmt_n(star_input),
    `STAR unique` = sprintf("%.2f%%", star_uniq_p),
    `STAR multi loci` = sprintf("%.2f%%", star_multi_p),
    `STAR too short` = sprintf("%.2f%%", star_short_p),
    `STAR other` = sprintf("%.2f%%", star_other_p),

  ) %>%

        caption = "Full alignment statistics for all three aligners.")
```

::: {.callout-important}
## `% mapped to too many loci` is now 0.00% — the multimappers are rescued, and this mattered

STAR runs with `--outFilterMultimapNmax 20 --outSAMmultNmax 1`, so a read hitting
several loci keeps its best alignment and carries `NH:i:` rather than being discarded.
`% mapped to multiple loci` therefore holds
`r sprintf("%.1f–%.1f%%", min(m$star_multi_p), max(m$star_multi_p))` of reads and
**`% mapped to too many loci` is 0.00% for every sample**.

Before 2026-09-30 the configuration was `--outFilterMultimapNmax 1` and these two
columns were the other way round: everything multimapping was dumped into "too many
loci" and fell through to the unanchored tail scan, which peeled 2–3 nt off an
unanchored read start and called it a `mixed` or `G` tail. That was **not** a uniform
background — the discarded fraction is genotype-structured, 4.2–7.3% in
DIS3L2/MOV10/WT against 10.7–27.7% in the TUT lines — so it inflated `mixed` from
0.94% (WT) to 12.81% (TUT4Δ), manufacturing a ~5× contrast rather than cancelling
across one. Correcting it flattened `mixed` to 0.94–1.31% across all six genotypes
while leaving the uridylation measurement unchanged (≤0.3 points in the strict set).

Full evidence in `implementation_plan.md` §14 and `docs/TAIL_CATEGORIES.md`.
:::

```{r align-commentary}
#| echo: false
#| results: asis

cat(sprintf(
"The transcriptome alignment is dominated by multi-mapping reads (%s–%s of all
R1 reads align to more than one transcript), which is expected: the index is
transcript-level and holds 670,670 sequences, so isoforms of the same gene
compete. The genome alignment
rate is consistently higher than the transcriptome rate, also expected, since
the genome is the larger and less redundant target.\n",
fmt_p(min(m$bt2_tx_multi / m$r1_raw)), fmt_p(max(m$bt2_tx_multi / m$r1_raw))))
```

# Duplication levels

Two different measurements, which should not be conflated:

- **Pipeline deduplication** — the rate reported by `tail_analysis`, collapsing
  reads on the R1 transcript coordinate. This is the one that affects the
  results.
- **fastp duplication estimate** — a sequence-identity heuristic computed on R2
  before alignment. Informational only; it never removes reads here.

```{r dup-chart}
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 8.5
#| fig-height: 7
#| fig-cap: "Duplication by sample, from two independent estimates."

dup_long <- m %>%
  select(pipeline_name,
         `Pipeline dedup (R1 coordinate)` = dedup_rate,
         `fastp estimate (R2 sequence)` = fastp_dup) %>%
  pivot_longer(-pipeline_name, names_to = "metric", values_to = "rate") %>%
  mutate(metric = factor(metric, levels = c("Pipeline dedup (R1 coordinate)",
                                            "fastp estimate (R2 sequence)")))

ggplot(dup_long, aes(x = rate, y = pipeline_name, fill = metric)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.8), width = 0.72) +
  geom_text(aes(label = fmt_p(rate)),
            position = position_dodge(width = 0.8),
            hjust = -0.15, size = 3, colour = INK_2) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = PAL_CAT[1:2], name = NULL) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = label_percent(), limits = c(0, 0.75),
                     breaks = seq(0, 0.6, 0.2),
                     expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.01))) +
  labs(title = "Duplication levels",
       subtitle = "Fraction of reads identified as duplicates",
       x = "Duplication rate", y = NULL) +
  theme_report()
```

```{r dup-commentary}
#| echo: false
#| results: asis

cat(sprintf(
"Pipeline duplication spans **%s to %s** across the twelve samples (median %s).
The fastp estimate runs consistently %s, which is expected — it counts identical
R2 sequences rather than collapsing on a mapped coordinate, and it sees reads
before UMI extraction.\n",
fmt_p(min(m$dedup_rate)), fmt_p(max(m$dedup_rate)), fmt_p(median(m$dedup_rate)),
if (median(m$fastp_dup) > median(m$dedup_rate)) "higher" else "lower"))
```

# Quality flags

Computed checks, not commentary. Each flags a sample worth a second look.

```{r flags}
#| echo: false

# within-genotype spread: a replicate at odds with its partner
flag_tbl <- m %>%
  group_by(genotype) %>%
  mutate(
    tx_dev   = bt2_tx_rate - median(bt2_tx_rate),
    star_dev = star_uniq_p - median(star_uniq_p)
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(
    depth_ratio = r1_raw / median(r1_raw),
    f_depth = ifelse(depth_ratio > 1.5 | depth_ratio < 0.67,
                     sprintf("depth %.2fx median", depth_ratio), ""),
    f_tx    = ifelse(abs(bt2_tx_rate - median(bt2_tx_rate)) > 10,
                     sprintf("tx rate %.1f%% vs %.1f%% cohort median",
                             bt2_tx_rate, median(bt2_tx_rate)), ""),
    f_star  = ifelse(abs(star_uniq_p - median(star_uniq_p)) > 10,
                     sprintf("STAR unique %.1f%% vs %.1f%% cohort median",
                             star_uniq_p, median(star_uniq_p)), ""),
    f_dup   = ifelse(dedup_rate > median(dedup_rate) + 0.15,
                     sprintf("dup %.1f%% vs %.1f%% cohort median",
                             dedup_rate * 100, median(dedup_rate) * 100), "")
  ) %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(flags = paste(Filter(nzchar, c(f_depth, f_tx, f_star, f_dup)), collapse = "; ")) %>%
  ungroup()

flag_tbl %>%
  filter(nzchar(flags)) %>%
  transmute(Sample = as.character(pipeline_name), Genotype = geno_disp, Flags = flags) %>%
  kable(align = "lll", caption = "Samples deviating from the cohort. An empty table means nothing tripped.")
```

```{r batch-check}
#| echo: false
#| results: asis

t4 <- m %>% filter(genotype == "TUT4")
if (nrow(t4) == 2) {
  cat(sprintf(
"## `T4_12_S4` — the batch-effect check\n\nIts sample index (`S4`) sits outside the
`S321`–`S331` block, suggesting a different sequencing run. Against its replicate
`T4_5_S321`:\n\n| Metric | `T4_5_S321` | `T4_12_S4` | Difference |\n|---|---|---|---|\n",
""))
  cmp <- data.frame(
    metric = c("Raw R1 reads", "Read length after fastp", "bowtie2 transcriptome rate",
               "bowtie2 genome rate", "STAR uniquely mapped", "Duplication rate"),
    a = c(fmt_n(t4$r1_raw[1]), t4$len_after[1], sprintf("%.2f%%", t4$bt2_tx_rate[1]),
          sprintf("%.2f%%", t4$bt2_gn_rate[1]), sprintf("%.2f%%", t4$star_uniq_p[1]),
          fmt_p(t4$dedup_rate[1])),
    b = c(fmt_n(t4$r1_raw[2]), t4$len_after[2], sprintf("%.2f%%", t4$bt2_tx_rate[2]),
          sprintf("%.2f%%", t4$bt2_gn_rate[2]), sprintf("%.2f%%", t4$star_uniq_p[2]),
          fmt_p(t4$dedup_rate[2])),
    d = c(sprintf("%+.1f%%", (t4$r1_raw[2] / t4$r1_raw[1] - 1) * 100),
          sprintf("%+d nt", as.integer(t4$len_after[2] - t4$len_after[1])),
          sprintf("%+.2f pp", t4$bt2_tx_rate[2] - t4$bt2_tx_rate[1]),
          sprintf("%+.2f pp", t4$bt2_gn_rate[2] - t4$bt2_gn_rate[1]),
          sprintf("%+.2f pp", t4$star_uniq_p[2] - t4$star_uniq_p[1]),
          sprintf("%+.1f pp", (t4$dedup_rate[2] - t4$dedup_rate[1]) * 100)),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(cmp)))
    cat(sprintf("| %s | %s | %s | %s |\n", cmp$metric[i], cmp$a[i], cmp$b[i], cmp$d[i]))
  cat("\n**How to handle a genuine batch effect is a scientific decision**, not something
this report adjusts for. The numbers are here so the decision is informed.\n\n")
}
```

"It carries %s raw R1 reads — **%.1f× the median** of the other eleven (%s). Any
raw-count comparison against it must be depth-normalised. It is also a single
replicate, so it supports no within-genotype variance estimate.\n",

# Provenance

## The legacy `t47_*` outputs came from `T47_5_S323`

```{r t47-provenance}
#| echo: false
#| results: asis

# The legacy STAR log (R2_aligned_to_masked_genome/t47_Log.final.out) was deleted with the
# rest of the 2026-09-21 intermediates on 2026-09-30, so this comparison can no longer be
# recomputed live. It is reproduced below as a record.
#
# It could not be recomputed even if the log were still present: three of the four counts
# depend on STAR's multimapper and score thresholds, which changed on 2026-09-30. Only the
# input-read count is parameter-independent, and that one is still checked against the
# current tables.

cand <- m %>% filter(genotype == "TUT4_TUT7")
legacy_input <- 6648364L          # from the 2026-09-21 log, recorded in implementation_plan.md
hit <- cand %>% filter(star_input == legacy_input)

cat(sprintf(
"The single-sample run of 2026-09-21 was configured as `sample: t47` over a file named
`t47_2_R1.fq`, which has since been deleted — so its provenance could not previously be
established, and the filename suggested `T47_12_S322` (the planned `t47_2`). The STAR
statistics settled it: the legacy log and **`%s`** agreed exactly on four independent
counts.\n\n", if (nrow(hit)) as.character(hit$pipeline_name[1]) else "T47_5_S323"))

cat("Measured 2026-09-24, when both the legacy run and the twelve-sample run used
`--outFilterMultimapNmax 1` and `--outFilterScoreMinOverLread 0.66`:\n\n")
cat("| Metric | Legacy `t47` | `T47_5_S323` | `T47_12_S322` |\n|---|---|---|---|\n")
cat("| Number of input reads | **6,648,364** | **6,648,364** | 6,171,374 |\n")
cat("| Uniquely mapped reads % | **30.50%** | **30.50%** | 28.85% |\n")
cat("| % mapped to too many loci | **34.21%** | **34.21%** | 34.49% |\n")
cat("| % unmapped: too short | **22.57%** | **22.57%** | 23.90% |\n\n")

cat(sprintf(
"Of those four, only the **input-read count** is independent of the STAR thresholds, and it
still discriminates against the current tables: `T47_5_S323` = %s, `T47_12_S322` = %s. The
other three moved when the parameters changed on 2026-09-30 (uniquely mapped is now %.2f%%
and too-many-loci %.2f%% for `T47_5_S323`), so they are shown above as the historical
measurement rather than recomputed here.\n\n",
fmt_n(cand$star_input[cand$pipeline_name == "T47_5_S323"]),
fmt_n(cand$star_input[cand$pipeline_name == "T47_12_S322"]),
cand$star_uniq_p[cand$pipeline_name == "T47_5_S323"],
cand$star_toomany_p[cand$pipeline_name == "T47_5_S323"]))

cat("So the legacy `R_output/t47_*` files are **`T47_5_S323`** — the planned `t47_1`, not
`t47_2`. The source filename was misleading. This matters when the deferred renaming
happens: `R_output/t47_final_big.rds` and a future `t47_1_final_big.rds` would be **the same
sample under two names**, which is worth resolving before either is used downstream.\n\n")
```

## Machine-readable outputs

```{r write-tsv}
#| echo: false

dir.create("logs/align", showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

# Step 8a deliverable: the pooled cross-sample alignment summary
aln_summary <- m %>%
  transmute(pipeline_name = as.character(pipeline_name), genotype,
            total_reads_R1 = r1_raw,
            bt2_transcriptome_rate = bt2_tx_rate,
            bt2_genome_rate = bt2_gn_rate,
            star_input_reads = star_input,
            star_unique_pct = star_uniq_p,
            star_multi_pct = star_multi_p,
            star_toomany_pct = star_toomany_p,
            star_unmapped_pct = star_short_p) %>%
  arrange(match(pipeline_name, rev(levels(m$pipeline_name))))

write.table(aln_summary, "logs/align/alignment_summary.tsv",
            sep = "\t", quote = FALSE, row.names = FALSE)

# the full metric set behind this report
full_out <- m %>% mutate(pipeline_name = as.character(pipeline_name)) %>% select(-geno_disp)
write.table(full_out, "reports/run_report_metrics.tsv",
            sep = "\t", quote = FALSE, row.names = FALSE)
```

Two machine-readable tables are written each time this report renders:

- `logs/align/alignment_summary.tsv` — the pooled cross-sample alignment summary.
- `reports/run_report_metrics.tsv` — every metric in this document, one row per sample.

by hand.\n\n", fpv))
